intro.title: Conditional Classes
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple React component that changes its visual style based on user interaction. You'll learn how to apply CSS classes conditionally using JavaScript logic within your JSX. The main technologies involved are React's JSX syntax, TypeScript for type safety, and the `className` attribute. This technique is essential for creating dynamic, responsive user interfaces that react to state changes.
intro.usecase: Conditional classes are essential for creating responsive, interactive UIs in real-world applications. In e-commerce sites, they highlight selected filters or indicate out-of-stock items with visual cues. Dashboard interfaces use them to show active navigation tabs, toggle between light/dark themes, or display real-time status indicators like 'online' or 'offline'. Form validations apply conditional classes to show error states on invalid inputs, while modals and notifications use them for smooth enter/exit animations.
